newsitem.title: USA: Fed seen adding via customers, may stay out.
newsitem.headline: Fed seen adding via customers, may stay out.

text.p: The Federal Reserve Bank of New York is expected by some Fed watchers to temporarily add reserves to the banking system on Tuesday via customer repurchase agreements.
However, some analysts think the New York Fed may refrain from open-market operations with two outstanding fixed system repos in place and federal funds trading below target.

"We are expecting the Fed to inject reserves with customer RPs," said economist Dana Saporta at Stone and McCarthy Research. "This would supplement the three-day and seven-day system RPs outstanding from Monday and Thursday (last week.)
Saporta expected "a moderate size customer RP operation," based on a remaining $2-billion daily add need through Wednesday, the end of the reserve maintenance period.
But MCM MoneyWatch senior economist Astrid Adolfson thought the Fed could stay out of the market.
"They have two large fixed system RPs outstanding. So, they may decide to wait until tomorrow and do an overnight system to clean it (add need) up," Adolfson said.
At 1050 EDT/1450 GMT, federal funds changed hands at 5-3/16 percent, below the 5-1/4-percent target.
